description: We are a student team passionate about space science, AI, and solving real-world problems using NASA data. Our goal is to build a meaningful and technically strong project for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, while learning and experimenting along the way.We believe the best way to learn is by building. We research, experiment, make mistakes, solve problems, and keep pushing until an idea becomes something real.
summary:
AstroShift is an open-source citizen science web platform built by Team ExploRangers to simplify multi-epoch infrared and astronomical FITS data analysis. Directly addressing the challenge of making complex space telescope archives accessible, AstroShift transforms raw NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) and SPHEREx mission datasets into an interactive browser-based research workspace.

To use AstroShift, users search a celestial target or sky coordinates in Target Explorer, upload multi-epoch FITS files into the Observatory for automatic World Coordinate System (WCS) alignment, and compare epochs in Science Lab using interactive Blink and Wipe sliders to spot brightness changes or moving objects—while asking AstroBot for real-time astrophysics guidance.

By eliminating heavy desktop software barriers, AstroShift empowers students, educators, and citizen scientists to explore time-domain astronomy and contribute to infrared discovery from any browser.
details:
AstroShift is an end-to-end citizen science web platform built by Team ExploRangers to simplify the exploration, astrometric alignment, and visual comparison of multi-epoch astronomical observations—specifically tailored for NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) and SPHEREx near-infrared survey datasets.

Users enter through an interactive 3D cosmos landing interface and follow a four-stage research workflow:
1. Target Explorer (Catalog Reconnaissance): Resolves celestial object names and sky coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination) in real time via the CDS Sesame service (querying SIMBAD, NED, and VizieR databases) to inspect target metadata before loading observation files.
2. Observatory (Multi-Epoch FITS Ingestion & Alignment): Allows users to upload multi-epoch astronomical FITS files (such as NASA/IPAC IRSA and SPHEREx datasets) captured on different dates. The backend automatically performs World Coordinate System (WCS) reprojection and astrometric image registration so frames taken across different epochs align accurately pixel-for-pixel.
3. Science Lab (Visual Temporal Comparison): Transforms those aligned multi-epoch FITS files into interactive visual comparison views using Blink (rapid frame alternation) and Wipe (split-screen comparison slider) modes, enabling users to spot flux variations, transient events, and moving objects across epochs.
4. AstroBot (AI Astrophysics Companion): An embedded AI assistant that guides users through FITS header metadata, infrared wavelengths, mission objectives, and time-domain analysis workflows in plain language.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Raw FITS datasets from space telescope archives traditionally require heavy desktop software installations, command-line environments, and custom scripting pipelines—creating a steep barrier for students and newcomers. AstroShift eliminates these technical hurdles by moving WCS astrometric registration and multi-epoch comparison into a zero-install, browser-based workspace. Its intended impact is to democratize time-domain astronomy, support STEM education, and empower students, educators, and citizen scientists worldwide to explore real NASA infrared data and contribute to transient and variability discovery.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Stack
• Backend & Scientific Processing (Python): Built with Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, and HTTPX, utilizing Astropy (FITS file parsing and WCS handling), Astroalign (automated astrometric image registration), NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and Pillow (astronomical image rendering), alongside the CDS Sesame API for real-time celestial coordinate resolution.
• Frontend & Visualization (JavaScript / JSX, HTML5, CSS3): Built with React 19, React Router, Vite, and Tailwind CSS, integrating Three.js (React Three Fiber & Drei), GSAP, and Lenis to power the interactive 3D cosmos experience and responsive multi-epoch Blink/Wipe canvas viewers.
• AI & Cloud Infrastructure: Powered by multi-model LLM integration (Google Gemini, Groq, and NVIDIA APIs) for AstroBot, version-controlled on GitHub (https://github.com/Andromed628/Astroshift), and deployed on Render. Super Intelligence (SI) tools were utilized for AstroBot's conversational astrophysics guidance and to accelerate code prototyping and documentation.

Resilient FITS Ingestion & Sample Test Files for Judges:
To provide frictionless testing without requiring judges to search external archives, two ready-to-use multi-epoch FITS test files (Frame A and Frame B) are linked under Space Agency Partner & Other Data.
• Extension-Agnostic Backend Parsing: Because astronomical FITS files begin with a readable ASCII header, web browsers and mobile devices frequently append ".txt" during downloads (saving files as .fits.txt). Rather than relying on fragile filename extension checks, AstroShift's backend uses Astropy (astropy.io.fits) to inspect the internal FITS header signature directly. This defensive engineering ensures zero upload failures across desktop and mobile browsers—judges can download both sample files and upload them straight into the Observatory workspace as Frame A (reference) and Frame B (target) with no renaming required.


Creativity & Design Considerations
Rather than presenting intimidating raw FITS header tables or static light curves, AstroShift pairs rigorous astronomical coordinate alignment with tactile visual comparison tools (Blink and Wipe) and conversational AI guidance. Our team prioritized cross-device accessibility (ensuring smooth performance on tablets, laptops, and low-bandwidth connections), modular REST API design for rapid server-side FITS processing, and transparent attribution of all NASA datasets, open-source libraries, and AI-assisted components.

Judges can download two sample multi-epoch FITS files from the links to immediately test Observatory alignment and Science Lab's Blink/Wipe comparison.
